===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:flowe<ety:from<enm:flowen>>|id=noun|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|flowe}}, from the verb (see below). The psychology sense “state of focus” was {{coin|en|Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi|in=1975|nocap=1|nocat=1}}.
[[File:Jõelähtme_jõgi._01.jpg|thumb|]]

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# Movement in people or things characterized with a continuous motion, involving either a non solid mass or a multitude.
# The movement of a [[real]] or [[figurative]] [[fluid]].
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|IV|48|Mr. Cooke at once began a tirade against the residents of Asquith for permitting a sandy and generally disgraceful condition of the roads. So roundly did he vituperate the inn management in particular, and with such a loud '''flow''' of words, that I trembled lest he should be heard on the veranda.}}
# {{lb|en|math}} A [[formalization]] of the idea of the [[motion]] of [[particle]]s in a [[fluid]], as a [[group]] [[action]] of the [[real number]]s on a [[set]].
#: {{uxa|en|The notion of '''flow''' is basic to the study of ordinary differential equations.}}
# The rising movement of the [[tide]].
# [[smoothness|Smoothness]] or [[continuity]].
#: {{uxa|en|The room was small, but it had good symmetry and '''flow'''.}}
# The amount of a fluid that moves or the rate of fluid movement.
#: {{uxa|en|Turn on the valve and make sure you have sufficient '''flow'''.}}
#: {{uxa|en|Other devices measure water '''flow''' in streams fed by melted ice.}}
# A flow pipe, carrying liquid away from a boiler or other central plant (compare with [[return]] pipe which returns fluid to central plant).
# {{sid|en|mental state}} {{lb|en|psychology}} A mental state characterized by [[concentration]], [[focus]]{{,}} and enjoyment of a given task.
#* {{RQ:Guardian|url=http://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/the-running-blog/2014/jan/14/achieve-state-flow-running-perform-best|title=How to achieve a state of flow when running|date=2014-01-14|author=Alex Lockwood|passage=The point about '''flow''' is that it is enjoyable. As research has shown "the more often athletes experienced '''flow''', the happier they were." But the second is that entering '''flow''' actually improves performance.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261019172729/https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/the-running-blog/2014/jan/14/achieve-state-flow-running-perform-best|archivedate=19 October 2026}}
# The [[emission]] of [[blood]] during [[menstruation]].
#: {{uxa|en|Tampons can be small or large, slender or thick. From “slender” to “super”, you can pick the size that matches your '''flow'''.}}
# {{lb|en|rap|_|music|_|jargon}} The ability to skillfully [[rap]] along to a [[beat]].
#: {{uxa|en|The production on his new mixtape is mediocre but his '''flow''' is on point.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|title=w:In da Club|artist=w:50 Cent|year=2003|album=Get Rich or Die Tryin'|passage=Now shawty said she feelin' my style, she feelin' my '''flow''' {{...}} / My '''flow''', my show brought me the dough / That bought me all my fancy things}}
# {{lb|en|software}} The sequence of steps taken in a piece of [[software]] to perform some action.
#: {{coa|en|login '''flow'''}}
#: {{coa|en|search '''flow'''}}

===Etymology 2===
{{etymid|en|etymverb}}
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:flowen|id=verb|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|flowen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|flōwan|t=to flow}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*flōan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*flōaną|t=to flow}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*plōw-}}, lengthened ''o''-{{glossary|grade}} form of {{m|ine-pro|*plew-|t=to fly, flow, run}}. 

Cognate with {{cog|stq|flouje|t=to flow}}, {{cog|fy|floeie|t=to flow}}, {{cog|nl|vloeien|t=to flow}}, {{cog|no|flo|t=to flow}}. Compare also {{cog|en|float}}. Not cognate with {{noncog|la|fluō}} despite similarity.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To move as a [[fluid]] from one position to another.
#: {{uxa|en|Rivers '''flow''' from springs and lakes.}}
#: {{uxa|en|Tears '''flow''' from the eyes.}}
#* {{quote-video game|en|developer=w:BioWare|title={{w|Mass Effect (video game)|Mass Effect}}|location=Redwood City|publisher=Electronic Arts|year=2008|genre=[[science fiction|Science Fiction]]|system=PC|scene=|isbn=9780784546642|oclc=246633669|passage={{w|Wrex}}: I need to get my blood '''flowing'''. Find me something to kill!}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[proceed]]; to [[issue]] [[forth]]; to [[emanate]].
#: {{uxa|en|Wealth '''flows''' from industry and economy.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=VII|217|signature=Ee|verso=yes|lines=1238{{ndash}}1239|Tho{{long s}}e thou{{long s}}and decencies that daily '''flow''' ¶ From all her words and actions, mixt with Love}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To move or match smoothly, gracefully, or continuously.
#: {{uxa|en|The writing is grammatically correct, but it just doesn't '''flow'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Dryden Aeneis||chapter=Dedication|183|{{...|But}}''Virgil'',{{...|who never attempted the Lyrick Ver{{long s}}e,}}is{{...|every where Elegant,}}{{long s}}weet and '''flowing''' in his ''Hexameters''.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To have or be in abundance; to abound, so as to run or flow over.
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Joel|3|18|18|signature=Ffff3|verso=yes|page=969|columns=1{{ndash}}2|{{...|¶ And it {{long s}}hall come to pa{{long s}}{{long s}}e}}in that day, ''that''{{...|the mountaines shal drop downe new wine, and}}the hils {{long s}}hall '''flow''' with milke,{{...|and all the riuers of Iudah {{long s}}hall flow with waters, and}}a fountaine {{long s}}hall come forth of the hou{{long s}}e of the {{smc|Lord}},{{nb...|and {{long s}}hall water the valley of Shittim.}}|“In that day{{...|the mountains will drip new wine, and}}the hills will '''flow''' with milk;{{...|all the ravines of Judah will run with water.}}A fountain will flow out of the Lord’s house{{nb...|and will water the valley of acacias. {{sqbrace|Or ''Valley of Shittim''}}}}|version=NIV}}
#* {{RQ:R. Chambers Wilson Burns|volume=II|page=cxv|passage=Were the joys that circle round the '''flowing''' bowl to be interdicted to him alone, the wittiest, the brightest, the most original, and the most eloquent of all the men of his day!}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To hang loosely and wave.
#: {{coa|en|a '''flowing''' mantle}}
#: {{coa|en|'''flowing''' locks}}
#* {{RQ:Federalist|LXVII|Concerning the Con{{long s}}titution of the Pre{{long s}}ident: A gro{{long s}}s Attempt to mi{{long s}}repre{{long s}}ent this Part of the Plan detected.|222|{{...|He has been {{long s}}hewn to us with the diadem {{long s}}parkling on his brow, and}}the imperial purple '''flowing''' in his train.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[rise]], as the [[tide]]; opposed to ''[[ebb]]''.
#: {{syn|en|come in|come up}}
#: {{uxa|en|The tide '''flows''' twice in twenty-four hours.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 4-2|IV|iv|93|2|line=125|The Riuer hath thrice '''flow’d''', no ebbe betweene:|The river hath thrice '''flow’d''', no ebb between;}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|computing}} To arrange (text in a wordprocessor, etc.) so that it wraps neatly into a designated space; to [[reflow]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To allow (a liquid) to flow.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1932|author=Carl Ernest Reistle|title=Paraffin and Congealing-Oil Problems|volume=340-349|page=45
|passage=The action is usually progressive, and as a certain amount of oil is '''flowed''' from the tubing it lowers the pressure on the remaining oil and liberates more gas, thus causing additional oil to flow from the tubing.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cover with [[water]] or other [[liquid]]; to [[overflow]]; to [[inundate]]; to [[flood]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cover with [[varnish]].
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[discharge]] [[excessive]] [[blood]] from the [[uterus]].

===Etymology 3===
{{ety|en|id=bog}}
{{unc|en}}. Perhaps from {{cog|non|flói|t=a large bay, firth}}, see {{m|en|floe}}. Compare {{cog|sco|flow|t=peat-bog, marsh}}, {{cog|is|flói|t=marshy ground}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|Scotland}} A [[bog]] or [[mire]], especially a rough, waterlogged one.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1794|author=John Sinclair|title=The Statistical Account of Scotland|volume=10|page=328
|passage={{...}} there are other extensive mosses in this district, commonly called flowes, which it is not probable ever will, or ever can be, converted into arable land. Some of these '''flowes''' are found to be 20, 25, or 30 feet deep, and are, besides, such a dead level, that the water has little or no descent; and even supposing they should be cast, or burnt to the bottom, standing pools of dirty water could only stand in their place.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1871|author=Alexander Boswell|title=Poetical Works|page=213
|passage=Ye'll stick in some '''flow''', Or, ye'll melt in a thow}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1896|author=Proudlock|title=Borderland Muse|page=8
|passage=Dandering o'er ferney knowes, [...] Springing o'er bogs an' '''flowes''', [...]}}
